reasons: Quantity matches: system.load.1 is the 1-minute load average, which corresponds to system.cpu.load_average.1m (gauge).

Aggregation differs: the Datadog query has no explicit space aggregator, so it defaults to avg across the in-scope hosts. The candidate uses sum(), which adds load averages across hosts and gives a different number.
Expected PromQL should aggregate with avg(), not sum(), keeping the single ungrouped series. Outcome translated is correct since the metric exists and no function is involved.
Unit: Datadog system.load.1 is unitless while the OTel metric is {thread}. Both are plain load counts, so this is not a scaling difference.
